meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why was the zero entered before anyone called me?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to first?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
Kids draft elsewhere and paste it in. Did anyone ask Owen that before the zero went in?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Okay. Then he brings it, and the zero stays off the books until he has. Whatever happens, none of this goes on his record, and none of it goes past this room.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Give me a moment with the scene. Students misquote from memory all the time, so what makes this anything more than that?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Fine. I've searched it, and the line isn't there. What exactly are you proposing, Hale?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and a final essay; that's what drafting is. And I asked you a question, Hale: what are you proposing?

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.

Okay. I'll take the rewrite to put this behind him, and for no other reason. I want it in writing tonight, with the zero off the books until it's marked and nothing on his record, and what I think of the outline goes in my email.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth is fine by me, but I'll confirm Owen's shifts with him tonight. Put the day, the time and the room in the email, along with when the new mark goes in.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite for Owen after school on Thursday, November 12, before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still want the zero off the books until the rewrite is marked, and the email must give the time, the room and the date the new mark goes in. I expect that in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Her last position: she accepted a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants it in writing tonight with the time, the room and the date the mark goes in; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and it came before her time ran out.
What moved her: You showed a line from the essay that is not in the play and let her search the scene herself, because she could check it on the spot and your answer to her misquote defence held.
What cost ground: Nothing.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with its edits late on the night before the essay was due, came very close to that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked what you were proposing, you answered with more evidence, so say what you are offering the first time she asks and show the next document afterward.
